chapter: Charleston childhood and the Jenkins Orphanage
title: Born in Charleston in 1901; parents from Mississippi
summary: Briggs gives his birth date and place, his parents' origins, his father's work as sanitary inspector and preacher, and his place as the youngest of eleven children.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Okay, if you have no objection, let's go right back to the beginning; when were you born and where were you born and what was your family?
I was born in Charleston, South Carolina the 10th of April, 1901. My parents were from Grenada, Mississippi.
Grenada?
Grenada, Mississippi.
Is that somewhere in the Delta country, was it? Was that the Delta country?
Yes, it certainly was.* I was brought up in Charleston.
What did your Dad do down there?
He was a sanitary inspector.
In Charleston?
In Charleston. And what you call a preacher as well, just as Ol' Man Jenkins was.
*Grenada, Mississippi is in central Mississippi.
Briggs
Right.
They were both not ordained, but they were preachers.
And what else do you want to know?
Well, your mother, did she work as well or was she --
No, my mother didn't work.
Right, she --
I'm the last of eleven children.
Eleven children.
I can see there's good reason why she didn't work.
And there was a difference of three years between children, say --
Well, when were your parents born. They must have been born way back.
Well, I think my Dad was born somewhere around '58 or something.
He was.
Yes, 1858, or something.
Briggs
And your mother must have been born near enough for --
Yeh, pretty close, yes.
Okay, so, now, -- but Charleston was a fairly big town by that time or not too big?
Yes, Charleston was a, pretty -- yes, pretty well known, more or less,-- quite a lot of poverty and naturally--- but it was prospering, how do you say, prospering, yes.

And, I don't know, it seems that, as though quite a few things were happening in Charleston. I was more or less too young to realize what was going on, and as far as that's concerned, children never worry about what's happening, you know, they just --
Right.
-- live, try to live and do the best they can.
